notes: REVIEW REQUIRED (A17): the coordinates rest on a geocoder source only. No official CERN or geodetic publication giving WGS84 coordinates for LHC Point 1 was reachable in this session (cds.cern.ch is behind bot protection; home.cern and atlas.cern state only that ATLAS 'sits in a cavern 100 m below ground near the main CERN site, close to the village of Meyrin').

summary.plain: The underground cavern at the edge of CERN's Meyrin campus where the ATLAS detector sits, about 100 metres below ground. It is one of the eight access points around the 27-kilometre Large Hadron Collider ring and the place where two of the LHC's proton beams are made to collide inside ATLAS.
summary.technical: LHC interaction point 1 on the CERN Meyrin site: the UX15 experimental cavern ~100 m below the surface housing the ATLAS detector, together with its surface buildings and the ATLAS control room.
